sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: In this lesson you put together what you already know and learn to choose: «I usually buy tinned tomatoes» or «I am buying a ready-made meal today». You also learn to say what hurts, what the weather is like and how to ask politely.

examples.en: I am buying a ready-made meal today.

sections.title: Usually — or now, for a while

blocks.text: If it's a habit, use the form from lesson 6: I often travel abroad. If it's happening now or only for a while — on this trip, today — use the form from lesson 9: We are staying at the seaside.

formula.text: now: who + am / is / are + action + ing

examples.translation: I go to other countries many times.

examples.en: We are staying at the seaside.
examples.translation: We're living by the sea for now.

examples.en: I am buying a ready-made meal today.

fixes.wrong: I buy a ready-made meal today.
fixes.right: I am buying a ready-made meal today.

drill.question: You usually cook, but today you got a ready-made meal. What do you say?
drill.optionA: I buy a ready-made meal today.
drill.optionB: I am buying a ready-made meal today.
drill.explain: today is about today, not a habit: am buying.

blocks.text: Often the sentence itself tells you which form to use. often, usually, once a week, twice a week mean a habit — no -ing. today, now mean right now — am / is / are + -ing.

examples.translation: I can't find my way many times.
I'm looking at the weather news now.

fixes.wrong: I swim one time a week.
I am swimming once a week.

drill.why: twice a week is a habit, so no -ing.

sections.title: need, know, agree — no am, no -ing

blocks.text: Some words almost never take -ing or am: need, know, agree. Even if it's true right now, just say I need, I know, I agree. And agree with someone needs with: I agree with you.

examples.translation: I must have a ticket there and back.
Milk is the one thing I need.
I have the address in my head.
I think the same as you.

fixes.wrong: I am need a bin bag.

drill.hint: One word is extra. Tap it.
drill.fix: agree is an action, no am: I agree with you.

blocks.text: To say part of your body hurts, use have with the problem: I have a sore throat. No am. With he and she, use has: She has earache, He has backache. Before earache, backache and toothache we usually don't put a.

fixes.wrong: I am have a sore throat.

sections.title: Small words: also, only, just, almost

blocks.text: also, only, just and almost go before an action: I also need bread, I only need milk. With the clip, they go after it: I am just looking, It is almost ready.
probably means «I think so». It goes after the clip: He is probably at home. perhaps means «maybe». It goes first: Perhaps he is on the bus. quite means «rather»: It is quite cold.

examples.en: Perhaps he is on the bus.

drill.why: After is, use probably; perhaps goes at the start.

blocks.text: For a time of day, use at: at nine, at lunchtime, at midnight. For «before», use before: before bedtime. For «during the day», use in the daytime. Time goes at the end of the sentence.

examples.translation: I walk in the middle of the day.
I read just before I sleep.

examples.en: We reach the station at nine.
examples.translation: We get to the station at nine o'clock.

blocks.text: For weather and temperature, use It is, as in lesson 1: It is quite cold, It is one degree, It is minus two. Don't leave out It.

sections.title: Polite questions: Can I…? Can you…?

blocks.text: To ask for something for yourself: Can I…? — Can I have your phone number? To ask someone to do something: Can you…? — Can you repeat that? To ask the price: How much does it cost? After can and does, the action has no to and no s.

examples.en: Can I have your phone number?

fixes.wrong: Can I to have your phone number?
fixes.right: Can I have your phone number?

blocks.text: Good morning is for the morning, Good afternoon for the afternoon, Good evening for the evening. Good night is not a greeting — you say it when you leave at night or go to bed.

fixes.wrong: I buy a ready-made meal today.
fixes.right: I am buying a ready-made meal today.

fixes.wrong: I am swimming once a week.
I am need a bin bag.
I am have a sore throat.

blocks.text: The main question in this lesson: habit or now? Habit — like lesson 6. Now or for a while — am / is / are + -ing. need, know, agree and «what hurts» — never with am.
Usually: I buy, I swim once a week. Now, today: I am buying. need, know, agree: no am. What hurts: I have, he has. Small words before the action or after the clip. Weather: It is…

examples.translation: I go to other countries many times.

examples.en: We are staying at the seaside.
examples.translation: We're living by the sea for now.
I have the address in my head.
